newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-OPENER FLOWER PROPS UP ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-OPENER FLOWER PROPS UP ZIMBABWE.

text.p: Opener Grant Flower propped up Zimbabwe with his second highest one-day international score of 90 in the triangular tournament match against South Africa on Saturday.
Zimbabwe were all out for 211 in 48.5 of their 50 overs in the day-night game but South Africa's success in restricting their opponents to a modest total was tempered by injury to Craig Matthews.
Paceman Matthews retired hurt after the seventh ball of the match, having sprained his ankle and ruptured a ligament in bowling his first delivery.
Matthews' injury will keep him out of cricket for three weeks. His replacement in South Africa's squad has yet to be named.

Opener Flower put on 51 for the second wicket with Alistair Campbell and 47 for the sixth wicket with Guy Whittall to give Zimbabwe's score a degree of respectability after winning the toss on a typically bland Centurion Park pitch.
The younger of the Flower brothers was eventually seventh out when he drilled a half volley from Allan Donald straight to Andrew Hudson at extra cover.
He hit eight boundaries from 126 balls, but fell one run short of his best one-day score, made against Pakistan in Quetta last year.
Paul Strang took up the reins when Flower left and smashed 39 from 41 balls, his highest score in limited overs internationals.
Strang fell to an express yorker from Donald, the pick of the South African bowlers with four for 37.
South Africa won the first tournament match last Thursday, beating India by 39 runs.
